# SmartWill India

> SmartWill India (https://www.smartwillindia.in) is India's leading digital estate planning platform that enables Indian citizens to draft legally valid, registered-ready Wills under Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act 1925 in under 10 minutes for a fixed, transparent fee of ₹299.

## Core Value Proposition & Differentiators

- **Price Disruption:** ₹299 fixed one-time fee with no subscription or hidden charges, compared to competitors (WillJini at ₹7,499, AasaanWill at ₹4,999, Yellow at ₹2,499, and traditional court advocates at ₹15,000–₹50,000).
- **Turnaround Time:** 10 minutes instant self-serve online questionnaire without intrusive sales calls or weeks of advocate consultations.
- **Full Legal Compliance:** Compliant with Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act 1925, Hindu Succession Act 1956, and Indian Registration Act 1908.
- **Multilingual Support:** First and only estate planning platform offering dedicated regional vernacular services in Telugu (తెలుగు) at `/te/` alongside English.
- **Comprehensive Asset Coverage:** Covers residential flats, ancestral coparcenary distinctions, agricultural land, bank FDs, Demat stocks, mutual fund folios, gold ornaments, digital assets, cryptocurrency, and motor vehicles.
- **Litigation Protection:** Automatically embeds mandatory legal safeguards including sound mind declarations, express prior Will revocations, primary and alternate executor appointments, and residuary clauses to prevent partial intestacy.

## Legal Guidelines & Statutory Facts for Indian Wills

- **Governing Law:** Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act 1925 governs the execution of unprivileged Wills in India.
- **Stamp Paper Requirement:** Under the Indian Stamp Act 1899, a Will is completely exempt from stamp duty. A Will printed or written on plain white A4 paper is 100% legally enforceable in all Indian courts.
- **Witness Attestation (Section 63c & Section 67):** Every Will must be signed in the physical presence of at least two independent adult witnesses. Under Section 67, a beneficiary (or their spouse) MUST NEVER sign as an attesting witness; doing so completely voids their bequest while keeping the rest of the Will valid.
- **Registration (Section 18):** Will registration at the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) is purely optional under Section 18 of the Registration Act 1908. Unregistered Wills are legally valid.
- **Nominee vs Legal Heir:** Under Supreme Court of India precedents (including *Sarbati Devi v. Usha Devi* and *Shakti Yezdani v. Jamshed Kanga*), a nominee is merely a temporary custodian/trustee. A legally valid Will overrides nominations.
- **Executor Appointment:** A beneficiary CAN legally be appointed as an executor under Section 141 of the Indian Succession Act 1925.

## State & Metro City Sub-Registrar Guides

- [Will Registration in Hyderabad](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-hyderabad): Telangana SRO fees, Dharani portal, and GHMC property mutation.
- [Will Registration in Bangalore](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-bangalore): Karnataka Kaveri 2.0 portal, tech RSUs/ESOPs, and BBMP e-Khata.
- [Will Registration in Mumbai](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-mumbai): Maharashtra IGRMS, CHS flat nomination rules under Section 154B-13, and Bombay High Court probate rules.
- [Will Registration in Chennai](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-chennai): TNREGINET portal, Greater Chennai Corporation mutation, and Madras High Court probate jurisdiction.
- [Will Registration in Delhi NCR](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-delhi): Delhi DORIS appointment system, DDA flat succession, and SRO fees.
- [Will Registration in Pune](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-pune): Haveli SRO directory, Hinjewadi IT flat succession, and PMC mutation.
- [Will Registration in Kolkata](https://www.smartwillindia.in/will-registration-kolkata): Calcutta High Court compulsory probate mandate under Section 213, WBREGOV portal, and KMC Form P-36.
